key_insight: The paper separates feature learning from graph structure by aligning a structure-conditioned GNN with an independent feature anchor, improving robustness to noisy or heterophilous edges.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more stable graph learning design for real-world networks where topology is unreliable, incomplete, or inconsistent with node attributes.
method: Anchor model learns structure-free node features via self-supervised reconstruction.
CSAG-GNN routes information between global spectral smoothing and local spatial discrimination using node-wise gating.
Cyclic alternating constrained optimization keeps the two views aligned and reduces representation drift.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports balanced performance gains and improved structural robustness on both homophilous and heterophilous benchmark datasets.
watch_item: The alternating bi-level optimization and dual-view alignment likely add training complexity and may require careful tuning for stable convergence.
paper_title: Structure-Feature Aligned Graph Learning via Alternating Constrained Optimization
